steps.title: Disinfect and sterilize coverslips
steps.instruction: In a fume hood dip each 12 mm coverslip in 70 % EtOH, place 4‑5 coverslips in a 35 mm Petri dish, lean on the lid and let EtOH dry for a few minutes; then expose each side to UV light for 20‑30 min (optional). For electrophysiology attach either an IBIDI cell‑culture insert (Cat. # 80209) or a Fisher glass cylinder (Cat. # 09‑552‑21) using Loctite Glass Glue applied sparingly along the edge; the insert or cylinder is removed after the coverslip is placed in the recording chamber.

steps.title: Poly‑D‑Lysine coating
steps.instruction: Add 20‑30 µl of 100 µg/ml Poly‑D‑Lysine (PDL, >300 kDa) to each insert or coverslip, incubate either overnight at 4 °C or 2 h at 37 °C, aspirate the PDL, rinse 2‑3 times with sterile water, air‑dry inside the biosafety cabinet, cover the dish with parafilm and store at 4 °C (use within 1 month).

steps.title: Prepare solutions
steps.instruction: Make three solutions: (a) Dissociation solution – 1 mg/ml Stemxzyme I + 0.1 mg/ml DNase I in HBSS (12 ml per DRG batch). Use stock Stemxzyme I 10 mg/ml (add 0.1 ml per ml of solution) and DNase I 4 mg/ml (add 25 µl per ml). (b) BSA 12 % (120 mg/ml) – dissolve 20‑50 ml in HBSS, shake gently (no vortex), filter‑sterilize with Steriflip (Cat. # SCGP00525) and aliquot 2‑3 ml into 15 ml conical tubes; keep at room temperature. (c) Culture media – BrainPhys supplemented with 1 % Pen‑Strep, 2 % SM1, 1 % N2, 1 % GlutaMax, 10‑20 ng/ml hNGF (stock 100 µg/ml) and 5‑10 ng/ml GDNF (stock 100 µg/ml).

substeps.instruction: Mix Stemxzyme I and DNase I into HBSS to reach 1 mg/ml and 0.1 mg/ml respectively.
Prepare 12 % BSA solution, filter‑sterilize, and aliquot.
Add supplements to BrainPhys as listed.

steps.title: Dissect DRGs (cold)
steps.instruction: Place dissected DRGs in a Petri dish containing Sylgard coated with sterile NMDG‑aCSF, secure them with several 25‑gauge needles, remove excess fat, connective tissue, meninges, epineurium and nerve roots in the same cold NMDG‑aCSF, and weigh the DRGs. Adjust the final volume of dissection solution after weighing if needed.

steps.title: Mince DRGs (cold)
steps.instruction: In a 35 mm Petri dish filled with sterile NMDG‑aCSF cut the DRGs into 0.4‑0.5 mm pieces (larger 1‑2 mm pieces are acceptable) and transfer the pieces to the dissociation solution in conical tube 1.

steps.title: First‑round enzymatic digestion
steps.instruction: Seal tube 1 with parafilm, place it on a nutating shaker at 60‑70 rpm and incubate at room temperature for 90‑180 min until tissue begins to loosen (visible fiber‑like threads). Digestion time depends on piece size and donor age.

steps.title: First‑round trituration
steps.instruction: Using wide‑bore fire‑polished Pasteur pipettes, perform 10‑15 gentle strokes per pipette tip size, starting with ~2 mm diameter, then 1.5 mm, then 1 mm; avoid bubbles and move to a smaller tip when tissue flows easily.

steps.title: Start second‑round digestion
steps.instruction: Collect undigested tissue with a Pasteur pipette, transfer it to tube 2 containing fresh dissociation solution, and continue enzymatic digestion at room temperature for 45‑90 min.

steps.title: Assess SGC coverage after round 1
steps.instruction: Place 50‑100 µl of the round‑1 suspension on a Petri dish, lay a 10‑12 mm coverslip on top, wait 1‑2 min for neurons to settle, and examine under a microscope. If >10‑20 % of neurons lack satellite glial cell (SGC) coverage, proceed; if most are still covered, add 2‑3 ml fresh digestion solution and incubate at 37 °C for 10‑20 min, then re‑assess.

steps.title: BSA gradient centrifugation
steps.instruction: Gently layer 2‑3 ml of the cell suspension onto 12 % BSA (avoid disturbing the gradient) and centrifuge at 500 g for 9 min at room temperature using slow acceleration and deceleration. If debris is abundant, first pass the suspension through a 100 µm cell strainer (repeat with additional strainers if clogging).

steps.title: Recover neurons and count viability
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant without disturbing the pellet, add 100‑200 µl BrainPhys media and resuspend cells. Mix 2‑3 µl of the suspension with 2‑3 µl of 4 % Trypan Blue, incubate 1 min, cover with a 10‑12 mm coverslip and count stained (dead) versus unstained (live) neurons. Calculate total neuronal count = ((stained + unstained) / µl of suspension added) × volume of BrainPhys added. Survival rate = (unstained / total) × 100 %. Typical round‑1 survival >90 %.

steps.title: Create round‑1 cell stock
steps.instruction: Dilute the resuspended cells to 5 cells/µl in culture media, aliquot into Eppendorf or screw‑cap tubes, store at room temperature, and replace half of the media twice weekly. Cells remain viable for at least 2 weeks.

steps.title: Plate cells on coverslips
steps.instruction: Plate 2‑4 coverslips per day. If using inserts or glass cylinders, pre‑flood the Petri dish with 3 ml culture media; otherwise add 10‑20 µl cell suspension to each coverslip, let cells adhere for 1‑2 h, then gently add 1 ml media (avoid disturbing cells). Optional: coat coverslips with 20‑30 µl of 1 µg/ml laminin in media, incubate 37 °C 30 min, discard excess laminin and add cells. If debris remains, let neurons sediment 3‑5 min, discard 60‑90 % of supernatant and replace with fresh media to maintain desired concentration.

steps.title: Culture cells
steps.instruction: Incubate plates at 37 °C with 5 % CO₂, replace half of the media with fresh solution every other day, and perform physiological recordings 1‑10 days after plating (or as planned).

steps.title: Second‑round processing
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 7 (trituration), 8 (second‑round digestion), 9 (SGC assessment), 10 (BSA gradient), 11 (recovery/count), 12 (stock), 13 (plating) and 14 (culture) for the second round; expect higher debris and lower survival than round 1.
